```{r}
library(REDCapCDMSTAT)
nx <- cdmstat_demo(dir = file.path(tempdir(), "stats"), reset = TRUE, actor = "sam")
```

## Wrangling longitudinal and repeating data

One call chooses how events and repeating instruments are laid out, and the
variable list shows what that choice makes available:

```{r}
long <- nx$shape("long", "drop")
wide <- nx$shape("wide", "collapse")
c(long = nrow(long), wide = nrow(wide))
v <- attr(wide, "variables")
head(v[v$type != "id", c("name", "type", "event", "label")], 12)
grep("^(n_|any_|max_)", names(wide), value = TRUE)
```

| `longitudinal` | `repeating` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `"long"` | `"drop"` | one row per subject and visit; repeating forms removed |
| `"wide"` | `"collapse"` | one row per subject; visit-varying fields become `field__event`; repeating forms summarised (`n_`, `any_`, `max_`) |
| either | `"only"` | the repeating-instrument rows themselves |

## Table 1 with guarded test selection

The arm is detected from the dictionary (a radio or dropdown field named
like `arm` or labelled "randomised"). The baseline variables are the
analysable fields at the first event, excluding identifiers, dates and free
text.

```{r}
t1 <- nx$table_one()
t1[t1$variable %in% c("age", "sex", "sbp", "hba1c", "pregnant"), c("label", "level", "Drug A", "Placebo", "p_value", "test", "rationale")]
```

- **Continuous variables** are tested for normality within each arm
  (Shapiro-Wilk). If normal, they're summarised as mean (SD) with a Welch
  t-test; if not, as median [IQR] with a Wilcoxon test.
- **Categorical variables** use a chi-squared test, or Fisher's exact test
  when any expected count is below 5.

That automatic choice suits **exploratory** analysis. For a **confirmatory**
analysis, the tests must come from the statistical analysis plan, and SAP
mode enforces that:

```{r}
try(nx$table_one(mode = "sap"))
nx$table_one(vars = c("age", "sex"), tests = list(age = "t.test", sex = "chisq"), mode = "sap")[, c("label", "level", "p_value", "test", "rationale")]
```

## Outliers that become queries

```{r}
o <- nx$outliers("weight")
o[o$outlier, ]
```

Scores are robust z-scores (from the median and MAD) within each visit, so
one extreme value cannot hide itself by inflating the standard deviation.
In the apps, clicking a flagged point raises the query.

## Trends by arm

```{r}
tr <- nx$trend("weight")
tr[, c("event", "group", "n", "mean", "lower", "upper")]
```

## Models

All models run on the shaped data. Formulas use the shaped column names.

```{r}
# ANCOVA: week-24 SBP adjusted for baseline (wide data)
nx$fit("sbp__week_24 ~ arm + sbp__baseline", "linear")[, c("term", "estimate", "conf_low", "conf_high", "p_value")]

# Logistic: any serious adverse event (repeating form collapsed per subject)
nx$fit("any_ae_serious ~ arm", "logistic")[, c("term", "odds_ratio", "ratio_low", "ratio_high", "p_value")]

# Cox: time to the primary endpoint
nx$fit("Surv(followup_days, event_occurred == 'Yes') ~ arm + age", "cox")[, c("term", "hazard_ratio", "ratio_low", "ratio_high", "p_value")]

# Mixed model for repeated measures (long data, record-level fields carried to each visit)
mm <- nx$fit("sbp ~ arm * redcap_event_name + (1 | record_id)", "mixed")
mm[, c("term", "estimate", "conf_low", "conf_high", "p_value")]
attr(mm, "random_effects")
```

The simulated drug lowers systolic BP by about 9 mmHg versus placebo at week
24, and the mixed model recovers it (the `armPlacebo:...week_24` term).

## Reproducibility

Each call above was logged. `nx$script()` returns a linear R script that
replays them, with the project connection read from the environment, never a
token:

```{r}
cat(tail(strsplit(nx$script(), "\n")[[1]], 12), sep = "\n")
```

To pin an analysis to a frozen, signed-off dataset, call
`nx$use_cut(cut_id, require_signoff = TRUE)` first. See
[Reports, CDISC and reproducibility](reports-cdisc.html).
